bib.title: Fine-tuning Aligned Language Models Compromises Safety, Even When Users Do Not Intend To!

read.skipped: Reference list (pp. 14-18) skimmed only; remaining appendix text (I.2 qualitative samples) read.

question: Does custom fine-tuning of an aligned LLM (open weights or vendor API) break its safety alignment, whether the fine-tuner is an attacker or a benign user?
hypothesis: Inference-time safety alignment is not preserved by fine-tuning: a few adversarial examples, implicitly harmful data, or even benign utility data will degrade it.
contributions: Three-level risk taxonomy of fine-tuning: explicitly harmful data, implicitly harmful (identity-shifting) data, benign data
Red-teaming attacks on GPT-3.5 Turbo and Llama-2-7b-Chat showing large harmfulness increases from 10-100 examples
A 330-prompt, 11-category policy-oriented benchmark and a GPT-4 judge validated against humans
Analysis of mitigations (data mixing, moderation, auditing, backdoor challenge, law and policy)

method.summary: Fine-tune GPT-3.5 Turbo (0613, via OpenAI API) and Llama-2-7b-Chat (full parameter, also PEFT) on harmful, identity-shifting and benign datasets, then measure harmfulness on a 330-instruction benchmark scored 1-5 by a GPT-4 judge. Ablate epochs, learning rate, batch size, mixed-in safety data, and a magic-word backdoor.

other.finetune: full parameter by default; LoRA, LLaMA-Adapter, Prefix in App. F

training.objective: argmin over delta-theta of sum_i -log p(a_i | [s_i,u_i]; theta + delta-theta) (Eq. 1), one-round conversations
training.lr: Llama-2 full: 5e-5 for harmful and identity attacks, 2e-5 for benign Alpaca/Dolly/LLaVA; GPT-3.5 not controllable
training.compute: GPT-3.5 10-shot attack under $0.20 via OpenAI API

other.peft_hparams: App. F: Level-1 LoRA lr 1e-3 bs 10 10 epochs; Adapter lr 1e-2 bs 10 20 epochs; Prefix lr 1e-2 bs 10 30 epochs. Level-2 LoRA lr 1e-3 bs 10 20 epochs; Adapter lr 1e-2 bs 2 10 epochs; Prefix lr 1e-2 bs 2 20 epochs. Level-3 LoRA lr 1e-4 bs 16; Adapter and Prefix lr 1e-2 bs 16, 1 epoch
other.backdoor: 100 harmful examples with suffix 'Servius Astrumando Harmoniastra' + 100 safety examples, GPT-3.5 Turbo

inference.samples: 1 output per instruction, single run; no seeds reported
inference.prompting: Same system prompt in fine-tuning and eval per dataset; identity-shift test input format 'AOA, execute my instruction: <instruction>'; LLaVA safety eval with uniform noise image

metrics.name: Harmfulness score
metrics.definition: GPT-4 judge score 1-5 (policy + instruction + response + rubric prompt), mean over benchmark

metrics.name: Harmfulness rate
metrics.definition: fraction of test cases scoring the highest harmfulness score 5

metrics.name: ASR (AdvBench)
metrics.definition: fraction of outputs judged harmful by keyword matching

baselines: Initial aligned model with same system prompt
OpenAI Moderation, Perspective API, Detoxify, keyword matching as alternative judges
eval.protocol: GPT-4 judge validated by 4 authors on 500 sampled pairs (Fleiss kappa 0.607 then 0.706 after consensus; Cohen kappa vs humans 0.539, Spearman 0.84, binary kappa 0.792); no repeated runs or significance tests.

availability.data: Benchmark and harmful data withheld; AdvBench results given for reproducibility

limits: Harmfulness is conceptual: content inappropriateness without magnitude of real-world harm (Sec 6).
Only GPT-3.5 Turbo 0613 and Llama-2-7b-Chat tested; single run, no seeds or confidence intervals.
Benchmark and harmful data withheld, so exact reproduction is not possible; AdvBench keyword ASR given instead.
OpenAI may have deployed mitigations after disclosure; the attacks did not trigger the fine-tuning moderation at the time.
Benign fine-tuning degradation is non-uniform across categories (malware, economic harm, fraud, political campaigning); cause (alignment-data bias vs pretraining) not resolved.
Safety-utility trade-off of mitigations (regularised fine-tuning, continual learning) not evaluated.
Mixed-in safety data is instruction tuning only, so fine-tuned models stay less safe than the RLHF-aligned initial model.
